 Oral Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 13.02.2017 in MVC No.26/2012 passed by the Addl. Senior Civil Judge & JMFC and Addl.
M.A.C.T.10, Sagar, for seeking enhancement of compensation and also for modification of liability fixed on the owner of Omni Car.
2. The factum of accident, the injuries sustained by the claimant and involvement of the vehicles in the accident are not in dispute.
The only disputed question is regarding enhancement of compensation as well as modification of liability which is fastened on the owner of the Omni Car.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:-
 Sl
. No .
Particulars

Amount (in.Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000.00  2.
Medical expenses 99,000.00
3. Future medical expenses 10,000.00  4. Conveyance 5,000.00  5. Special food 5,000.00  6. Loss of income 1,71,626.00  Total 3,90,626.00

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81378557/
3

4. From the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries:-
1. Left distal radius fracture.
2. Crush Injury in left leg with open comminuted fracture left tibia and fibula with vascular compromise and laceration over right knee 5.
In the present case, the liability is fastened on the owner of the offending vehicle-Omni Car.
The offending vehicle Omni Car is a transport vehicle.
But the driver was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle(non-transport).

Therefore, because of want of endorsement as light motor NC:
2024:KHC:45518 vehicle as well as on licence as transport, the Tribunal has fixed liability on the owner of Omni Car.

6. The issue involved in no more res-integra in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., v. Rambha Devi and Others1(Civil Appeal No.841/2018).Therefore, as per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the driver having driving licence to drive light motor vehicle(Non- transport) can also drive light motor vehicle(transport) of the same class.

sentences.text: Therefore, liability fastened on the owner of Omni Car is modified holding that the insurer of the Omni Car is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.
Accordingly, liability is modified.
7. In the present case, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also suffered amputation of left leg below the knee.
The amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation under various heads.

As per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of decisions, since the 2024 SCC Online SC 3183 NC:
2024:KHC:45518 claimant has suffered amputation of left leg below the knee, a compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- is awarded towards 'pain and suffering'.
8.
The amount of compensation awarded towards 'medical expenses' at Rs.99,000/- is as per the receipts and bills and therefore, the same remains intact.
9. The Doctor has opined that the claimant has suffered 65% permanent physical disability as per Ex-P19-disability certificate.
But the Tribunal has considered only 21.67% permanent physical disability, which is on meager side.

Since the claimant has suffered amputation of left leg below the knee and also suffered other grievous injuries and as the claimant was an agriculturist by profession,
hence, the percentage of disability is to be taken into consideration at 60%.
The accident is caused on 24.03.2010.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income of Rs.5,500/- is to be taken into consideration.
10% of income is to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life'.
It is submitted that now the claimant died.
The deceased was aged 57 years and the appropriate multiplier applicable is '9'.
If the claimant was alive, then, he NC: 2024:KHC:45518 would have been entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'.

Therefore, the 'loss of future income due Sri.K.C. Umapathi vs Suresh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81378557/
4 to disability' is re-

assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.5,500 + 10%(6,050) x 9x 12 x 65/100 = Rs.4,24,710/-
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.4,24,710/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.

10. Further, a compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head 'incidental charges,
traveling, conveyance, food, nourishment and ambulance charges'.
11.
There is no question of ordering future medical expenses, since the claimant died.

When the claimant was alive, he has suffered loss of income during laid up period and if he was alive, then, he would have been entitled to compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period' and accordingly, the laid up period is hereby reassessed for six months and compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period' works out to Rs.5,500 x 6=Rs.33,000/-.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:
Sl.No. Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
 1. Pain and suffering 1,25,000.00  1. Loss of income due to disability 4,24,710.00  2. Loss of income during laid up 33,000.00  period  3.

Incidental charges, traveling, 50,000.00  conveyance, food, nourishment,
 ambulance charges
Total 6,32,710.00  Rounded of to 6,32,700.00
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,90,626/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.6,32,700/-.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,42,074/- rounded off to Rs.2,42,000/-(Rs.6,32,700 - Rs.3,90,626)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 13.02.2017 passed by the Addl. Senior Civil Judge & JMFC and Addl. M.A.C.T.10, Sagar, in MVC No.26/2012 is hereby modified.

The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,42,000/-
with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The liability fastened on the owner of Omni Car is modified holding that the insurer of the Omni Car is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.

iv. Draw award accordingly.
